criterion_notes.c1: The study surveys urban households that already have piped water service in their homes and examines their consumer/behavioural decision to drink tap water directly from the public network rather than household or community access to water service (although service continuity and water pressure are included as operational covariates).
criterion_notes.c2: Fails BOTH the plain wording of Criterion 2 and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading. Under the plain wording, no legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance factor is empirically measured or analysed: Mexican drinking-water standards (NOM-127-SSA1-1994, NOM-179-SSA1-2020, NOM-230-SSA1-2002) are mentioned only as background context, and effective regulation appears solely as a policy recommendation in the abstract and conclusions, while the actual explanatory variables are subjective perception of water purity, past waterborne illness, operational continuity and pressure, household sociodemographics, and municipal dummy variables. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading, no rule-type mechanism governing service access (eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation/tenure rules, tariffs/cost-recovery, discretion/accommodation, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure) is studied.
criterion_notes.c3: Quantitative empirical study using primary data from a 2018 probabilistic household survey of 1,800 dwellings (N = 1,648 in econometric estimation) analysed with a recursive bivariate probit model.
criterion_notes.c4: The two dependent variables modelled are (1) the behavioural decision to drink water directly from the tap (bb_agua) among already-connected households and (2) subjective user satisfaction with the water service (satisff), rather than an access, connection, availability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion outcome (continuity and pressure enter only as explanatory variables for satisfaction).
criterion_notes.c5: Population and unit of analysis (households/respondents in dwellings across three Mexican municipalities, N = 1,800 surveyed / 1,648 analysed), exposures (satisfaction, perceived water quality, illness history, continuity, pressure, sociodemographics, municipality), outcomes (drinking tap water and service satisfaction), and study design (cross-sectional survey with recursive bivariate probit regression) are clearly specified.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish with an English abstract; Spanish is readily readable/translatable for full methodological assessment per Criterion 10.

evidence_quotes.quote: Most of the urban population in Mexico does not drink tap water despite having access to that service in their homes. This paper quantitatively analyzes key factors that explain this decision in three metropolitan areas

El modelo de este trabajo se instrumentó en dos ecuaciones: la primera intenta explicar la decisión de beber (1) o no beber (0) agua de la llave en función de las siguientes variables: satisfacción con el servicio de agua (satisff); percepción de la calidad del agua (agua_pura); antecedente de enfermedad relacionada con el agua en algún habitante de la vivienda (enfermedad)

La segunda ecuación define la satisfacción con los servicios (satisff), en función de las variables: percepción de la calidad del agua (agua_pura); continuidad diaria del servicio del agua (agua_continua); una presión adecuada del agua de la llave (agua_presion); número de años residiendo en la vivienda actual (antig_viv); y dos variables dicotómicas para registrar si la vivienda se encuentra en el municipio de La Magdalena Contreras (mun_1) o en Centro (mun_3).
Una regulación efectiva en aspectos operativos como la continuidad del servicio y una presión adecuada del agua, son condiciones necesarias para promover el uso efectivo del servicio.
La encuesta se aplicó a 600 viviendas en cada municipio, y la base de datos completa incluye 1800 observaciones.

raw_response.exposure: User satisfaction with water service, perceived organoleptic water quality (pure and crystalline), household history of waterborne illness, daily service continuity, water pressure problems, years of residence in the dwelling, car and internet availability, respondent sex, and municipal location dummies
raw_response.outcome: Household behavioural decision to drink water directly from the tap (bb_agua) and subjective satisfaction with the water service (satisff)
raw_response.population_and_sample: Urban households with piped water service in three municipalities across three Mexican metropolitan areas: La Magdalena Contreras (Mexico City), Monterrey (Nuevo León), and Centro (Villahermosa, Tabasco); 2018 two-stage cluster probability survey of 1,800 dwellings (600 per municipality), with N = 1,648 valid observations in the econometric model
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E03 (wrong exposure; also fails c1 and c4). Using a 2018 survey of 1,800 connected urban dwellings in three Mexican municipalities, Aguilar-Benitez (2024) estimates a recursive bivariate probit model of households' behavioural decision to drink tap water directly from the public network and their subjective satisfaction with water service. No legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance factor is empirically examined under either the plain wording of Criterion 2 or the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading: official water-quality standards are mentioned only in background context and effective regulation is raised only as a concluding policy recommendation, whereas the actual explanatory variables are perceived water purity, past waterborne illness, operational continuity and pressure, household sociodemographic traits, and municipal dummies. Moreover, surveyed households already have piped water access and the modelled outcomes are consumer tap-water drinking behaviour and satisfaction rather than service access or connection.
raw_response.study_design: Cross-sectional household survey (2018) analysed with a recursive bivariate probit econometric model
